issues.legal_issue: An unregistered lease document for a one-year term cannot be used to prove a lease from year to year on the basis of its annual-rent terms.
material_facts: The rent document stated a one-year term and annual rent payable in advance, but was not registered.
The tenant relied on the document’s annual-rent terms to argue that the tenancy was from year to year.
issues.conclusion: The document could not be used as evidence of a lease from year to year based on annual rent; it evidenced a lease for one year, which ended on expiry of that term.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act and Section 17 of the Registration Act, the document could not establish a lease from year to year without registration. The tenant cited Sajid Mia Majumdar v. Abdul Sattar Gani, Babulal Somalal v. Kantilal Hargovindas, and Chittiapalli Mathai v. Chittilapalli Kochouseph; the Court did not rely on those decisions as the basis for its ruling.

predicates.eviction_appeal: A tenant appealed an order granting eviction on the ground of rent arrears.
predicates.lease_document_unregistered: The parties' lease document was not registered.
predicates.document_claimed_yearly_tenancy: A party relied on the document's annual-rent terms to claim a tenancy from year to year.

issues.definition: When an eviction appeal involves an unregistered lease document relied on to claim a yearly tenancy, the document is not evidence of a lease from year to year.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant who remains after a one-year lease expires must pay rent month to month, and eviction for arrears is sustainable when the tenant does not tender the full arrears at the first hearing.
material_facts: The one-year lease expired while the tenant remained in the premises.
The tenant tendered only part of the rent claimed and did not pay the rent due for at least two months after the lease expired.
The lower courts found that the tenant had not tendered the whole amount of arrears on the first day of hearing.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was in arrears and had not tendered the whole amount due on the first day of hearing, so the eviction order was properly granted under Section 13 of the East Punjab Rent Restriction Act.
issues.legal_principle: After the one-year lease expired, the tenant, even if holding over, was liable to pay rent month to month as contemplated by the Rent Act, with rent payable in the succeeding month before its end. Under Section 13 of the East Punjab Rent Restriction Act, failure to tender the whole arrears on the first day of hearing supported eviction. The Court relied on its application of these statutory provisions and did not cite an earlier case as the basis for this ruling.

issues.definition: When a tenant appeals an arrears-based eviction order after remaining in the premises beyond a fixed-term lease, and fails to tender all monthly rent arrears at the first hearing, the eviction order is sustained.
